# BakeNN 1.0.0

BakeNN 1.0 stabilizes the static batch-one INT8 AOT compiler contract. It
accepts supported FP32 PyTorch models and supported fully-quantized static INT8
TFLite models on the host, then emits model-specialized standalone C11 without
shipping a model interpreter, FlatBuffer parser, heap allocator or target-side
floating-point fallback.

Highlights:

- versioned C/C++ firmware ABI, numerical profiles and manifest schemas;
- deterministic PTQ and strict TFLite semantic validation;
- an explicit TFLite AveragePool raw-code profile verified against LiteRT's
  built-in reference resolver rather than approximated with native rounding;
- Python integer reference, portable C and selected backend differential gates;
- transactional artifact generation with file and manifest-payload hashes and
  source provenance;
- portable C, direct CMSIS-NN and direct ESP-NN source closures under explicit
  capability and selection policies;
- reproducible memory reports, cross-build evidence and scoped physical-board
  benchmark bundles.

Evidence note: the historical nRF52840 and original-ESP32 runs retain reports,
recorded artifact hashes and UART/size logs, but their exact measured ELF/map
bytes were not archived. The release evidence manifest records this limitation
instead of substituting a later local rebuild. Future measurements must attach
their exact binaries with the evidence builder's `--artifact` option.

The intentional product constraints remain static shapes, batch one and one
public model input/output. Dynamic models, automatic float fallback, arbitrary
custom TFLite operators and full TFLM operator parity are outside the 1.0
contract.
